summary: Heinrich Plütschau was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied theology at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1702 to 1705 and later held a post there.

Philosopher Heinrich Rickert studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1884–1885) and the University of Strasbourg (1885–1888). He held posts at the University of Freiburg (circa 1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (circa 1916–1932).
Heinrich Rückert worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena from circa 1845 to 1852 and at the University of Breslau from circa 1852 to 1875.
Heinrich Schenkl studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1876 to 1880. He later held posts at the University of Graz (circa 1892–1901) and the University of Vienna (circa 1901–1919).
Heinrich Schliemann was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock in circa 1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Zurich and Berlin under Bernhard Hirzel, Franz Bopp, and others. He held multiple posts at the University of Zurich, including Ordinarius für Sanskrit und vergleichende Sprachforschung (1864–1889).

Indologist Heinrich Stönner studied at Marburg under Karl Friedrich Geldner, Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Emil Sieg, and Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel (PhD 1901). He served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, directing its Indian Department (1925–1931).
Indologist Heinrich Uhle studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1863 to 1868 under Hermann Brockhaus, earning a Dr. phil. From 1868 to 1911, he taught classical languages at the Kreuzschule.

Heinrich Wenzel specialized in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Jena, Tübingen (PhD under Rudolf von Roth), Strasbourg, Oxford, and Leipzig (under Georg von der Gabelentz). He also studied under Friedrich Max Müller, Heinrich August Jäschke, and Léon Feer.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Tübingen, Strasbourg, and Berlin under Rudolf von Roth, Albrecht Weber, and others. He held posts at Berlin, Greifswald, Heidelberg, Balliol College, and Columbia University.

Heinrich von Stietencron specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at London, Munich under Helmut Hoffmann, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University and the University of Tübingen, serving as Lehrstuhlinhaber at Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.
Heinrich von Wlislocki, who worked in linguistics and Indology, studied under Sámuel Brassai at Franz Joseph University from 1875 to 1879, where he completed his Ph.D.

Heinz Bechert was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz under Helmut Hoffmann and Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Saarland and Mainz before serving as Chair of Indology at Göttingen (1965–2000).

Linguist Heinz Kronasser studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Graz under Paul Kretschmer and Erich Frauwallner. He later held posts at the University of Graz, the University of Vienna, and the University of Würzburg.
Indologist Heinz Kucharski studied at the University of Hamburg in 1938. He served as the Director of the Indienabteilung at the Grassi Museum from circa 1958 to 1984.

Heinz Mode worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying in Berlin, Colombo, Visva-Bharati, and Basel under G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer. He served as Professor of Oriental Archaeology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1948–1978).

Heinz Zimmermann was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Zurich, Freiburg, and Basel. He held posts at the University of Zurich (1971–1979) and the University of Lausanne (from 1977; ord. Professor 1981).

Heleen De Jonckheere works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her doctorate at Ghent University (2016–2020) and has held posts at the University of Chicago (2021), University of Toronto Mississauga (2021–2024), and SOAS (2022).

Helen Baroni works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt. She held a post at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa from circa 1993.

Helen Hardacre specializes in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at Vanderbilt and the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith (1990–1992), and Harvard (from 1989).
